title: Ear-EEG motor execution dataset from Wu et al 2020
description: This dataset contains ear-EEG and scalp-EEG recordings from six healthy right-handed subjects performing a motor execution (fist clenching) task with left- and right-hand movements. Data were collected simultaneously from scalp and in-ear electrodes to evaluate the feasibility of ear-EEG for motor task classification. The dataset is a BIDS-formatted derivative generated using MOABB from the original data of Wu et al. (2020).
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a Neuroscan SynAmps2 system with 122 channels (112 EEG, 10 misc) at a sampling rate of 1000 Hz, using a standard_1005 montage, Ag/AgCl electrodes, scalp reference and ground, and online bandpass filtering (0.5-100 Hz). Subjects performed left-hand or right-hand fist clenching in response to visual arrow cues, with trials of 4 s duration, in a synchronous offline paradigm.
